questions.stem: What is the primary function of an operating system?

options.text: To manage computer hardware and software resources.
To serve as a programming language.

questions.explanation: The primary function of an operating system is to manage computer hardware and software resources, ensuring efficient operation and resource allocation.

distractorRationale.a: Option b is incorrect because providing internet connectivity is a function of networking software, not the OS itself.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is misleading as the OS does more than just run applications; it manages resources too.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect because an OS is not a programming language but rather a platform for running programs.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a thread?

options.text: A lightweight process that can run independently.
A separate program that runs without any process.
A complete program that requires its own memory space.
A type of hardware component in a computer.

questions.explanation: A thread is considered a lightweight process that can run independently and shares resources with other threads in the same process.

distractorRationale.a: Option b is incorrect as threads cannot run independently without being part of a process.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is misleading because threads share memory space with other threads in the same process.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect since a thread is a software construct, not a hardware component.

questions.stem: What state is a process in when it is waiting for I/O operations to complete?
questions.explanation: When a process is waiting for I/O operations to complete, it is in the Waiting state, indicating it cannot proceed until the I/O is finished.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because a Running state means the process is currently executing.
distractorRationale.b: Option b is misleading as the Ready state indicates the process is ready to run but not currently executing.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect since Terminated means the process has completed execution.

questions.stem: Virtual memory allows processes to execute even if they are larger than the physical memory available.
questions.explanation: True. Virtual memory enables the execution of processes that exceed the physical memory limits by using disk space as an extension of RAM.
